content.title: About
content.content: Stewed pork, Puerto Rican style is a traditional dish from Puerto Rico made with pork pieces slowly simmered in a fragrant sauce of tomatoes, garlic, onion, sweet pepper, olive oil, vinegar and characteristic spices such as oregano, cumin and adobo. The result is a rich, slightly sweet flavor with a gentle tang.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The stew is often served with rice, beans and fried plantains.
The adobo sauce used in the recipe comes from the Spanish word “adobar” meaning “to marinate”.
In Puerto Rico the dish is traditionally cooked in a cazuela – a clay pot that retains heat and deepens flavor.
Pork shoulder or neck cuts are preferred for their tenderness after long cooking.
Some regional variations add a splash of coconut milk for extra creaminess.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Pork provides a complete source of protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron from pork supports normal hemoglobin levels and helps prevent anemia.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The stew supplies thiamine, riboflavin, niacin and vitamin B12, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: A modest amount of monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats contributes to heart‑healthy nutrition when eaten in moderation.

items.title: Antioxidant spices
items.content: Oregano, cumin and garlic are rich in antioxidants that combat free radicals.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The sauce often contains soy sauce or added salt, so people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Excessive intake may raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Spice allergies
items.content: Some individuals may be sensitive to cumin, oregano or garlic.

items.title: Thorough cooking required
items.content: Pork must be fully cooked to eliminate the risk of salmonella and trichinella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the stew hot, typically alongside boiled rice, beans, fried plantains or a vegetable side. A squeeze of lime or fresh cilantro adds brightness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the stew to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3‑4 days. For longer keeping, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Reheat until it reaches 75 °C before serving.
